question: Question: break each GR00T stage down by % integer vs floating-point instructions used.
method: ncu (Nsight Compute) SASS executed-instruction-class counters over one fp16 inference per stage engine, run under sudo on-board. Metrics: smsp__sass_thread_inst_executed_op_{integer,fp16,fp32,fp64}_pred_on.sum, smsp__sass_thread_inst_executed.sum (total), sm__inst_executed_pipe_tensor.sum (HMMA). INT=integer; FP=fp16+fp32+fp64 (CUDA-core arithmetic); OTHER=total-INT-FP (memory load/store, control, conversion, movement). Kernels bucketed matmul vs glue by name. Engines = the same fp16 builds from $GVRB_WORK/onnx used for the compute-vs-glue sweep.
HEADLINE: On NVIDIA, a GR00T stage's instructions are NOT majority-integer and NOT majority-fp-arithmetic -- the single largest class is usually OTHER (memory movement + control), and the tensor-core matmul is done in ~1% or less of instructions as HMMA (0.09-1.24%). FP (arithmetic) outweighs INT 1.6-3.9:1, and the INTEGER work concentrates in the GLUE kernels (addressing/layout/indexing), not the matmul -- the same glue that compiler fusion hides.

int_matmul_vs_glue_pct.note: INT% within matmul-kernels vs glue-kernels -- integer work is consistently HIGHER in glue.

key_findings: Three-way split, not binary: OTHER (memory+control) is the largest class on Thor LLM/DiT (56-61%) and substantial everywhere. The matmul MACs are a few million HMMA instrs (0.09-1.24% of total) -- most matmul-kernel instructions just move tiles.
FP >> INT in arithmetic (1.6-3.9:1 every stage/board). The compute wants floating-point.

INTEGER work lives in the GLUE: glue-kernel INT% > matmul-kernel INT% on every stage (Thor DiT 29.6 glue vs 11.2 matmul; Orin LLM 33.2 vs 18.1). Integer = addressing, layout, indexing, quant -- the same glue fusion hides.

'fp16 engine' != 'fp16 instructions': Thor runs lots of fp32 (ViT 37%!) for norm/softmax accumulation + matmul epilogue; Orin runs more fp16 (LLM 45%). The fp16:fp32 split is TRT-version/arch dependent -- the robust cut is INT / FP / OTHER.

coverage.measured: Thor (Blackwell sm_110), Orin (Ampere sm_87) -- ncu SASS counters, run as root 2026-10-09.
coverage.rtx5090: n/a direct: ncu 2024.3.2 predates Blackwell sm_120 ('Failed to load Nsight Compute CUDA modules'). Thor (also Blackwell, same TensorRT family) is the nearest stand-in, but it is not a measurement of the 5090: the compute-vs-glue record shows the two architectures choose different tactics for the same ViT (64% vs 90% 'compute').

w4a16_weight_only_int4_llm_thor.question: Question: wouldn't int8/int4 weights show up for the LLM? Built W4A16 (weight-only int4) GR00T LLM on Thor from llm_w4a16_int4.onnx (85 DequantizeLinear, no QuantizeLinear) and profiled vs fp16.
w4a16_weight_only_int4_llm_thor.engine_size: 300 MiB vs fp16 1.15 GB (3.84x smaller; weights memory 311 MB = packed int4 + fp32 block-scales; int4 genuinely honored, not upcast)
w4a16_weight_only_int4_llm_thor.FINDING: int4 weights show up as INTEGER (on-the-fly unpack: shift/mask), nearly doubling the integer share (all 16->32%, glue 19->52%). The matmul STILL computes in fp16 (weight-only int4 dequantized before MatMul; NO int8 arithmetic / no IMMA int tensor ops). Total instructions ~7x higher (4.27e10 vs 6.19e9) -- on-the-fly dequant of every weight each forward. So W4A16 trades 3.8x less weight memory (bandwidth) for ~7x more instructions (dequant), and the extra work is INTEGER. Win when memory-bandwidth-bound (LLM decode); costly when compute-bound. Directly answers 'where do int weights show up': as integer unpack in the glue, not as int matmul. True int8 ARITHMETIC would need W8A8 (int8 activations too) -> IMMA ops.

caveats: Absolute INT/FP/OTHER split is compiler(TRT-version)+arch dependent (Thor vs Orin diverge, esp OTHER and fp16:fp32); the INVARIANTS are: INT is a minority (12-22%) and lives in glue; FP dominates arithmetic; OTHER(memory) is large; HMMA is ~1% or less of instrs (Orin LLM 1.24%). Orin ViT had one kernel error (ncu rc=9); re-parsed with nan-hardened parser, kernels≈483 (representative).
_correction_2026-10-12: Headline prose corrected to the record's own counts: HMMA is 0.09-1.24% of instructions (Orin LLM 1.24%, so not '<1%'); FP:INT ranges 1.6-3.9:1 across stage/board pairs (not '~2-3:1'). Counts unchanged.
